name: _PyEval_ExceptionGroupMatch
reason: exceptionGroupMatch mirrors :2263-2348 in order: None gives (None, None); a full PyErr_GivenExceptionMatches match gives the group or the egWrap oracle for the PyTuple_Pack/_PyExc_CreateExceptionGroup/traceback steps (stated), rest None; a non-matching group calls getattr(split) then the call with match_type (PyObject_CallMethod), requires PyTuple_CheckExact (exactTupleItems?, a tuple subclass refused) with the %.200s 'T.split must return a tuple, not U' message, then size >= 2 with 'got tuple of size n', and takes items 0 and 1 unchecked (:2339-2340); ExceptionGroupMatchRules pins every branch, so a body skipping either tuple check, wrapping a group or always answering (None, exc) fails, and the refuted bytecode-eg-match-handled runs the unchecked-items branch (bug YAML present).

name: _PyEval_FormatAwaitableError
reason: The am_await NULL test (:3497) is no __await__ in the type's MRO and not a coroutine (the coroutine type, coro_as_async at Objects/genobject.c:1386-1391, is the only builtin model type with am_await), then the oparg 1 __aenter__ / oparg 2 __aexit__ TypeErrors with %.100s of tp_name and nothing otherwise; GetAwaitableRules' third conjunct pins all five outcomes, so a body that ignored oparg, swapped the messages or replaced the error for a type with __await__ fails.

name: _PyEval_GetANext
reason: The PyAsyncGen_CheckExact fast path (:3563-3565) is not mirrored, and getANextImpl tests am_anext through callDunder, which sees only heap classes, so an async generator object (GenKind.asyncGen in the model, am_anext = async_gen_anext, Objects/genobject.c:1833-1838) gets "'async for' requires an iterator with __anext__ method" where CPython returns its asend awaitable; the rest (the call, _PyCoro_GetAwaitableIter, _PyErr_FormatFromCause setting __cause__ and __context__ of the new TypeError) is mirrored and pinned, but the first branch of the body and the commonest operand are outside the model.

name: _PyEval_GetAwaitable
reason: getAwaitableImpl mirrors :3645-3667: _PyCoro_GetAwaitableIter, on failure _PyEval_FormatAwaitableError whose TypeError replaces the error if it raises one (_PyErr_Format) else the original, then PyCoro_CheckExact with FRAME_SUSPENDED_YIELD_FROM (frameState 2, genYf) raising RuntimeError 'coroutine is being awaited already'; GetAwaitableRules pins the non-coroutine result, both coroutine cases and both error cases, so a body that skipped the awaited-already check or always kept the original error fails (builtin awaitables lacking __await__ are _PyCoro_GetAwaitableIter's model, its own row).
